messages:
maya: heads up — noticed a new latency tail in prod around 03:20 UTC. correlates with requests that do function/tool returns with structured JSON (big arrays). throughput drops ~18% and p95 jumps 230ms. attaching quick notes.

ajay: ugh. is this the same pause we saw when stop-token arrived mid-kv?

maya: seems related but different flavor. when tool returns are emitted we see repeated decode-pauses: decode loop yields until tool finishes, KV cache kept alive, but the batch formation holds other streams longer because stop-token heuristics try to resolve structured endings.

ryan: can you paste the perf trace snippet?

maya: sure — from a 3-min window:
```
kernel_single_stream: 42%
kernel_multi_stream: 18%
kv-lookup: 10%
decode-idle-wait (tool-pause): 22%
queue-hold-window: 8%
```

carmen: that decode-idle-wait number is huge. looks like batches are waiting for tool output to finish before dispatching next token slices.

maya: exactly. my hypothesis: structured returns often contain literal strings that include stop-like tokens or long JSON quoting; our stop-token detection does an eager check which triggers a pause+finalize flow early, but other queued streams remain attached to that batch formation window. net effect = poor packing + kernel choice flips to multi-stream kernels that are slower for our workload.

ajay: did kernel selector pick different kernels during those spikes?

maya: yes — logs show a fallback to multi_stream kernel because the estimated sequence-length distribution widened (some tool-call streams balloon). multi_stream has worse latency for small seqs.

ryan: quick mitigation idea: mark tool-calls / structured-output streams with a separate queue class (low-priority, long-tail) and avoid bundling them with short chat streams. also add a per-request token_budget_hint that prefers single-stream kernels when pause-probability > X.

carmen: good. additional tweak: relax eager stop detection when we see open JSON/object brackets in last 32 tokens — treat as soft-stop and allow token_budget to finish chunk, so we avoid premature finalize that holds batch. basically increase the holdwindow for flagged streams.

maya: I ran a safe experiment on canary:
- route tool-call responses to queue "tool-long-tail" (separate worker pool)
- set token_budget_hint=96 for flagged streams
- stop-eager disabled for streams with trailing "{\n" or "[" sequences
Result: p95 latency down 160ms, throughput +9% for mixed workload.

perf-bot: perf snapshot (canary) 2026-03-16T03:45Z: total tokens/sec +8.7%, p95 -160ms, kernel-switches down 38%.

ajay: nice! any downsides? memory usage or KV cache churn?

maya: small increase in reserved KV memory on tool pool (~3%), but KV miss rate went down. main trade-off is complexity: telemetry needs to mark tool-relative signals earlier so routing can happen before batch formation.

ryan: next steps: 1) add `is_toolcall` flag to request metadata + propagate to routing; 2) implement token_budget_hint in SDK + server-side enforcement; 3) tune stop-token heuristics to be JSON-aware; 4) add a kernel-selection override when pause_probability > threshold.

carmen: will create follow-up RFC and small rollout plan. rough perf rollback plan too.

maya: filing the canary results and logs in the perf board. tagging @ryan to own rollout and @ajay for kernel selector changes. thanks all :thumbsup:
